questions.question: What does schema (type) validation check?
options: Whether the content makes business/logical sense
Whether each extracted field has the correct structural shape/type (e.g. is a date a valid date, is amount a number)
Whether the model's confidence score exceeds a threshold
Whether the source document was OCR'd correctly

questions.question: An invoice's line items are all well-typed numbers, and the stated total is also a valid number, but they sum to £450 instead of the stated £500. What catches this?
options: Schema validation, since it checks all numeric fields
Semantic (business-rule) validation, via an explicit cross-field check
Nothing catches this — it's an unavoidable extraction error
The model's confidence score, which would automatically flag it

questions.question: Why is 'it validated against the Pydantic model, ship it' an incomplete stopping point for a team?
options: Pydantic models can't validate numeric fields
Schema validation passing only proves the extraction is well-formed, not that it's correct
Pydantic validation is deprecated in favor of JSON Schema
It means the extraction definitely contains a fabricated value

questions.question: In Pydantic, what construct typically implements cross-field semantic validation after individual field validation passes?
options: A `@model_validator` that runs after field-level validation and checks relationships between fields
A `@field_validator` applied to each field independently
The JSON Schema `type` keyword
A separate database migration script

questions.question: How do semantic validation error messages connect to retry-with-error-feedback?
options: They don't connect — retries only use schema validation errors
A specific message like 'line items sum to £450, stated total is £500' is exactly the actionable feedback the retry loop needs, unlike a generic 'validation failed'
Semantic validation errors are used only for logging, never for retries
Retry-with-error-feedback only applies before any validation runs

questions.question: Why does semantic validation scale with effort rather than tooling?
options: Business rules are domain-specific and have to be hand-enumerated for each extraction schema; there's no generic way to auto-derive them
Semantic validation requires a GPU cluster to run
It can be fully auto-generated from the JSON Schema definition
It only applies to financial documents, so effort is always minimal
